Check that an open session is still valid

Source: R/sessions.R
aa_user_session_valid.Rd

Called periodically (every session_check_seconds) so that blocking, deletion, role demotion and session termination take effect for a user who is already logged in, not only at the next login. A session is invalid if the user was deleted or blocked, the role in the database differs from the role in the session, or the token of this session was revoked (password reset, "end all sessions").

Usage

aa_user_session_valid(conn, login, role, token = NULL)

Arguments

conn

Database connection.

login

User login.

role

The role the user logged in with.

token

Autologin token of this session (auth$token()) or NULL if the session has no token (for example, autologin is disabled): then the token is not checked.

Value

A list: valid (logical), reason ("ok", "deleted", "blocked", "role_changed", "token_revoked", "check_failed") and role (the current role from the database or NULL).

Details

If the database cannot be read, the session is considered valid (reason = "check_failed") so that a database failure does not kick out all users; access is not widened, because no password is checked.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
check <- aa_user_session_valid(conn, auth$user()$login, auth$user()$role,
auth$token())
if (!check$valid) auth$logout(reason = check$reason)
} # }
